newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Berisha renews backing for Albania force.
newsitem.headline: Berisha renews backing for Albania force.

text.p: President Sali Berisha voiced new support for a multinational force to intervene in Albania on Friday after Italy asked the U.N. Security Council to authorise troops to safeguard aid to the anarchic Balkan state.

Jan de Marchant et d'Ansembourg, a Dutch diplomat leading a mission of European relief and security experts to Albania, said after meeting Berisha: "We asked him if he thought it (a foreign force) was useful and he did."
Berisha believed "the majority of the people would have no problem with this", d'Ansembourg told reporters. "Some people might but he did not expect this to lead to difficult situations."

Much of the south of the former communist state is ruled by rebels and armed gangs after protests against the collapse of savings schemes in recent months spilled over into an insurrection and calls for the right-wing Berisha to stand down.

United Nations Security Council members met informally late on Thursday night in New York to consider an Italian request to send a force to help protect humanitarian aid shipments like flour and medicines to Europe's poorest country.

Greece, France, Spain, Portugal, Austria, Turkey and Romania have expressed willingness to take part. Italy has estimated that about 2,500 personnel would be deployed initially, with another 2,500 in reserve.

D'Ansembourg, whose mission includes European Union representatives and experts from the OSCE security group and the Council of Europe, said he understood the U.N. would meet "again in New York on Monday or Tuesday on the issue of a security presence here".
Albania has repeatedly urged the quickest possible action to reopen supply lines and protect ports but d'Ansembourg reckoned it was realistic to expect a U.N. decision by the end of next week.

Meanwhile, Albanian police were investigating the killings of about 18 people in a shootout in central Albania on Thursday night, the worst bloodletting in two months of crisis, an interior ministry source said.
D'Ansembourg said Berisha mentioned the killings, referring to "armed bands".
The ATA news agency said an angry group of locals shot dead 16 armed people to avenge the killing of a local leader in Levan. Five badly shot and mutilated corpses lay in the local morgue.
The killings added to a death toll of already well over 100 people. Most military depots have been looted and prisoners released. Most foreign nationals were evacuated this month.
In one sign of hope on Friday, the first Red Cross relief truck since the crisis erupted crossed into the south of the country from Greece to test perilous road routes.
"They've reached the southern town of Gjirokaster and are distributing aid there," said Amanda Williamson of the International Committee for the Red Cross. "So far so good".

The truck, accompanied by two jeeps and carrying 10 tonnes of basic food like flour and sugar, aims to supply hospitals, orphanages and old people's homes. The vehicles turned back at the border on Thursday after an aborted first attempt.

Greek officials in Athens said that a group of about 2,000 Albanians protested outside the Greek consulate in Gjirokaster on Thursday about visa restrictions. About 300 tried to break in, firing in the air and throwing tear gas.
There were no reports of injuries.
Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino reiterated that the priority was to restore order but told Italy's Corriere della Sera newspaper that it was hard to predict when.

"Our police have no more uniforms, they have no helmets, no bulletproof vests. They have no adequate means of moving about in areas where it is urgent for them to intervene," he said. "Every Albanian is armed."
The Vienna-based Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) on Thursday asked the U.N. to consider endorsing a force comprising volunteer nations.

In a sign of the weak grip of the central authorities, the self-styled "salvation committee" in the southern town of Vlore was holding talks on the crisis on Friday with political groups from north and south.
